content:
A graph question is a reading test in disguise. The mathematics is rarely deep — but the paper wants exact coordinates, exact scale, exact story. Children who slow down for ten seconds here outscore faster classmates. Below sits a free IMO Class 8 Introduction to Graphs online test — 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation under every answer. Eight out of ten is the score to beat.

What the IMO asks from Introduction to Graphs in Class 8

  • Plotting points and reading coordinates in the first quadrant.
  • Points on the axes: (x, 0) and (0, y).
  • Line graphs: temperature, rainfall, growth over time.
  • Linear graphs from tables — cost vs quantity, interest vs time.
  • Distance–time journeys: speed, stops and returns.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Coordinates read (x, y): RIGHT first, then UP. (3, 5) and (5, 3) are different places.
  • Every point on the x-axis has y = 0; every point on the y-axis has x = 0.
  • Three collinear points are the cheap safety check that a "linear" graph really is linear.
  • On a distance–time graph, a horizontal stretch means STOPPED — and steeper means faster.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Swapping the x- and y-coordinates while plotting.
  • Misreading values between gridlines when the scale is 1 square = 5 units.
  • Joining discrete data points into a continuous line where no in-between values exist.

quiz.title: IMO Class 8 Introduction to Graphs Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 8: Introduction to Graphs

questions.q: The abscissa of a point is -8 and the ordinate is -3. The point lies in which quadrant?
questions.explanation: The abscissa (x-coordinate) is -8 and the ordinate (y-coordinate) is -3. Both coordinates are negative, so the point (-8, -3) lies in the third quadrant.

questions.q: Point P(2a - 7, 3a + 5) lies in the second quadrant. Which of the following is the valid range for a?
questions.explanation: For a point to lie in the second quadrant, its x-coordinate must be negative and y-coordinate must be positive. So 2a - 7 0 gives a > -5/3. Combining these: -5/3 < a < 7/2.

questions.q: A point in the fourth quadrant is 13 units from the origin. If its abscissa is 5, its ordinate is:
questions.explanation: Let the ordinate be y. Then √(5² + y²) = 13, so 25 + y² = 169, giving y² = 144 and y = +/-12. Since the point is in the fourth quadrant, y < 0. So y = -12. (This uses the 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple.)

questions.q: The distance of the point (a, a + 1) from the x-axis is twice the distance of the same point from the y-axis. If a > 0, the value of a is:
questions.explanation: Distance from x-axis = |a + 1| = a + 1 (since a > 0 implies a + 1 > 0). Distance from y-axis = |a| = a. Given a + 1 = 2a, solving gives a = 1.

questions.q: A graph passes through the points (1, 3), (2, 5), and (3, 7). The y-coordinate when x = 0 is:
questions.explanation: The y-values increase by 2 for each unit increase in x, so the relationship is y = 2x + 1. Verify: when x = 1, y = 3; x = 2, y = 5; x = 3, y = 7. All correct. When x = 0, y = 2(0) + 1 = 1.

questions.q: A straight line on a graph passes through (-2, 7) and (4, -5). The y-coordinate when x = 1 is:
For what value of k are the points (1, 2), (3, 6), and (5, k) collinear?
questions.explanation: Slope from (1, 2) to (3, 6) = (6-2)/(3-1) = 4/2 = 2. For collinearity, slope from (3, 6) to (5, k) must also be 2. So (k-6)/(5-3) = 2, giving k - 6 = 4, hence k = 10.

questions.q: A linear graph passes through (-2, 9) and (4, -3). The value of y when x = 7 is:
A linear graph passes through (2, 3) and (6, 11). The sum of the x-intercept and y-intercept of this line is:
questions.explanation: Slope = (11 - 3)/(6 - 2) = 8/4 = 2. Equation: y - 3 = 2(x - 2), so y = 2x - 1. The y-intercept is -1 (set x = 0). The x-intercept is found by setting y = 0: 0 = 2x - 1, x = 1/2. Sum = 1/2 + (-1) = -1/2.

questions.q: A taxi charges a flat fee of Rs 50 plus Rs 12 per km. From the fare-distance graph, the fare for a 15 km ride is:
questions.explanation: The fare equation is y = 12x + 50, where x is distance in km and y is fare in Rs. For x = 15: y = 12(15) + 50 = 180 + 50 = Rs 230.
